name: – Li Andersson – Amendments by the committee responsible – separate votes – Am 29
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the Member States
part_text: Member States should promote inclusive labour markets open to all by putting in place effective measures to eliminate every form of discrimination and ensure equal opportunities, particularly for groups underrepresented in the labour market and with due attention to regional and territorial dimensions. Member States should modernise their social protection systems to provide adequate, accessible, effective, efficient and sustainable social protection for all, throughout all stages of life, fit to the needs of an ageing population. They should foster social inclusion and upward social mobility through quality employment as a primary route out of poverty, support intergenerational fairness and a fair balancing of support across age groups, fight poverty and social exclusion, particularly child and in-work poverty, and address inequalities, including through the design of their tax and benefit systems, assessing the distributional impact of policies, while tackling discrimination in all its forms. Complementing universal approaches with targeted ones can improve the effectiveness of social protection systems. Member States should enhance the transparency and uptake of social protection benefits, including through the ethical and safe deployment of digital tools, and paying due attention to the digital divide. Particular support should be provided to vulnerable households and workers that are most affected by the green and digital transitions, and by uneven impacts of climate change and increases in the cost of living, including housing, transport and energy costs. Member States should take steps to close gaps in access to social protection for workers, including workers in platform and other atypical or non-standard forms of work and the self-employed, as an integral component of ensuring job quality.
